name: gaul
why: An old genetic algorithm library with example programs, a classic door into evolutionary computation.

brief.what_it_is: GAUL (Genetic Algorithm Utility Library) is an open source C programming library, released under the GNU General Public License, for building applications that use evolutionary algorithms. It provides data structures and functions for handling the data that serial and parallel evolutionary algorithms need. It also includes some non-GA stochastic optimisers for comparison or local search, such as hill-climbing, simulated annealing, and differential evolution, and much of its functionality can be reached through a simple S-Lang interface. The homepage lists the current version as devel-0.1849 with examples-0.1849. The input is a problem you encode as chromosomes and a fitness function, and the output is an evolved population.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it is 'designed to assist in the development of code that requires evolutionary algorithms.' The stated current aims are documentation, examples and test cases for the open-source release, with wrappers for languages other than C/C++ planned.
brief.how_it_works: Per the homepage, GAUL offers Darwinian, Lamarckian or Baldwinian evolutionary schemes, steady-state and generation-based GAs, and an island model, with multiple simultaneously evolved populations. It is chromosome-datatype agnostic, with common chromosome types built in, plus most usual crossover, mutation and selection operators and hooks for user-defined operators. Parallelism is available through MPI, OpenMP 2.0, pthreads, or a forked-process model.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install command. It says the main development platform is Linux with gcc, that it should be fairly easy to build on any POSIX system, and that it uses GNU maketools for portability. It reports successful use on RedHat Linux, FreeBSD, Solaris and IRIX, and says it can compile on Microsoft Windows with a few minor features disabled. MPI, OpenMP and pthreads support are optional parallel backends, and the S-Lang scripting interface is an optional layer. The brew formula's executable is gaul_diagnostics, but the homepage does not describe that program.
brief.standout: It is a long-lived, feature-dense GA library that covers many evolutionary schemes and also bundles comparison optimisers (Tabu Search, Simulated Annealing, Simplex, Differential Evolution) in one C library. It also ships a large set of example programs, which is the classic entry point the scout notes point to.
brief.status: Unclear from the homepage. The version string is devel-0.1849, the copyright runs 2000-2022, and the last press release listed is from 22 April 2005. The page has no explicit last-commit or release date, and the 'Latest Changes' link was not followed. The sourceforge development link and documentation link contain misspelled domains ('souceforge'), which suggests the site has not been carefully maintained, but that is an inference, not a stated fact.
brief.caveats: The homepage says GAUL 'is still under heavy development, and therefore is unlikely to be bug free.' Windows builds have some features disabled. Commercial modifications need separate terms from the author. The development home and documentation links on the page use the misspelled domain 'souceforge.net' and 'gaul.souceforge.net', so they may not resolve. The docs were not fetched, so no commands could be verified beyond the homepage. The homepage is a classic-looking HTML site with no code samples.
quotes: It is designed to assist in the development of code that requires evolutionary algorithms.

Trivial to extend using external code via the built-in code hooks.
